title: Gate state names the run that produced it
description:
Record, on each issue's gate state, the id of the latest run recorded for that gate, so the latest run is addressed from the issue record instead of being found by scanning runs.

## Background

`GateState` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:400-408`) holds a status, an actor and a timestamp, but not the run that produced it. Every reader that needs an issue's latest run of a gate therefore lists runs and selects one. The only conversion from a recorded run to a gate state is `gate_state_from_run` (`commands/gate_check.rs:225-246`), called by gate evaluation (`gate_check.rs:969`, `:1521`) and by lifecycle prechecks (`commands/mod.rs:2950`). A manual gate write replaces the state wholesale (`commands/mod.rs:1719-1723`), and a newly required gate is seeded at `commands/mod.rs:1647`.

`GateState` is built by struct literal in `domain/types.rs` tests (`:2296-2573`), `domain/queries.rs:871`, `output.rs:3075`, `validation/graph.rs:3180`, `visualization.rs:518`, `commands/template.rs:1237`, `commands/mod.rs:3627,3878`, `repository_state/mutation.rs:1452,1460,1942,1951`, `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:1703,1711`, `tests/fast_issue/transition_graph_enforcement_tests.rs:656` and `tests/fast_rules/example_rulesets_tests.rs:865`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GateState` has a `last_run: Option<GateRunId>` field. A record without the field decodes with `None`, and `None` is not serialized, so an issue record whose gates were never run serializes to the same bytes as before.
- [hard] REQ-02: A gate state derived from a recorded run carries that run's id. Gate evaluation and lifecycle prechecks both produce it through `gate_state_from_run`, in the same plan that records the run.
- [hard] REQ-03: A manual gate status write keeps the gate's prior `last_run`, and a newly required gate starts with none.
- [hard] REQ-04: A unit test proves that evaluating a gate twice leaves `last_run` naming the second run, and a test proves that a manual status write leaves `last_run` unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: Each recorded gate run's id is stored on the issue's gate state for that gate.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One optional field, one producer function, and a mechanical literal sweep.

title: Gate captures hold only the evaluated issue's latest runs
description:
Make gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation's precheck-history capture request the evaluated issue's latest run of each gate by path, so the mutation image never holds another issue's runs.

## Background

A checker that consumes run history (`checker_consumes_run_history`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:589-597`) receives the latest run of its gate on the evaluated issue (`compact_run_history_for_context`, `commands/gate_check.rs:252-266`). To find it, three captures list the whole `gate-runs/` root and take every run record into the image, then parse each one and keep those whose `issue_id` matches:

- gate evaluation: `discover_gate_run_results` (`commands/mod.rs:2048-2069`) called at `commands/gate_check.rs:806`, parsed by `captured_gate_runs` (`gate_check.rs:273-318`);
- precheck planning: `captured_precheck_plan` (`commands/mod.rs:622-680`, parse and filter at `:661-679`);
- validation's precheck-history capture: `commands/validate.rs:503-505`.

All three go through `captured_gate_run_result_paths` (`repository_state/mutation.rs:524-549`). The capture budget is 512 MB (`commands/mod.rs:235`), so the whole-root capture is also a future hard failure.

The issue record's gate state names the latest run of each gate (`GateState.last_run`), so the run record path is known from the issue record alone (`VirtualPath::gate_run_record`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation's precheck-history capture request, for each history-consuming gate on the evaluated issue, only the run record that the issue's gate state names. None of them lists the `gate-runs/` root.
- [hard] REQ-02: `discover_gate_run_results` and `captured_gate_run_result_paths` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test shows that evaluating a history-consuming gate on one issue captures no run record of another issue, with other issues' runs present, and that the checker still receives the evaluated issue's latest run of that gate.
- [hard] REQ-04: A gate with no recorded latest run passes the checker an empty run history, and `compact_run_history_for_context` sanitizes the one captured run without selecting among runs.

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: Gate captures request the evaluated issue's latest run of each gate by path and list no gate-run root.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three capture sites switch to one per-gate path request built from the issue record.

description:

title: Reusable verdicts are found through a per-key verdict record
description:

title: This repository's gate runs are rewritten into the per-issue layout
description:
Rewrite this repository's recorded gate runs once into the per-issue layout, with each issue's latest run named on its gate state and a verdict record for each reusable verdict, so no run history or cited run id is lost.

## Background

`.jit/gate-runs/` holds about 4,700 flat run directories (`gate-runs/<run-id>/result.json`), owned by about 980 issues. 584 runs carry an inputs digest over 395 distinct `(gate, digest)` keys, 123 runs are reused verdicts in the old provenance shape, and 92 run ids are cited in `dev/`, `docs/` or issue records. The released binary reads runs only at `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json`, takes the latest run of a gate from `GateState.last_run`, finds reuse through `gate-runs/verdicts/<gate-key>/<inputs-digest>.json`, and requires `source_issue` on a reused verdict. There is no migration reader.

Issue records are serialized canonically: sorted keys, two-space indentation, no trailing newline (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:576-597`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A script under `dev/active/f8a6b298-history-independent-reads/` moves each run record to `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json`, adds `source_issue` to each reused verdict, sets `last_run` on each issue's gate states from the run with the greatest `(started_at, run_id)` for that gate, and writes one verdict record per `(gate, digest)` key naming the latest qualifying run. Run bytes are otherwise unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: The script is idempotent: a second run changes no byte.
- [hard] REQ-03: The run count before equals the run count after, every run is reachable from its issue's directory, every cited run id still resolves, and repository validation passes.

title: Each lease is one record under one lease sequence
description:
Store each issue's lease in its own file, published by one lock-load-change-publish sequence, so reading or changing one lease reads only that file and an interruption leaves the prior or the next lease.

## Background

Each append rescans the log for the next sequence number (`get_next_seq`, `:959-976`). title: Captures and redo records refuse whole-log access
description:
Make the capture layer refuse a whole read of the event log and the redo record refuse a rewrite of it, so mutations can only probe the log's end and append to it.

## Background

`CaptureSpec::discover_paths` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:566-578`), and `CaptureSpec::new` through it, accept `VirtualPath::EVENTS` as a whole path; only `discover_tail` (`:581-589`) reads its bounded end. Repository deltas reject any non-append action on the log, but `RedoRecord::new` (`storage/redo_record.rs:110-130`) checks only path overlap, so a record could put or delete the log. Tests that capture the log whole: `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:1137`. Every production mutation already captures only the tail.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CaptureSpec::new` and `discover_paths` return a capture error for `VirtualPath::EVENTS`; the log is captured only through `discover_tail`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `RedoRecord::new` returns an error for a put or delete at the event log; the log changes only by the positioned event append.
- [hard] REQ-03: One test owns each refusal, and no other test captures the log whole.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: The capture layer and the redo record admit only a tail probe and an append on the event log.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two constructors gain one refusal each.

title: Default search reads no history file
description:
Exclude history files from `jit search` when no file selection is given, using one declaration of the history paths.

## Background

`jit search` with no `--glob` runs ripgrep over the whole data root (`crates/jit/src/search.rs:116-150`, CLI call site in `main.rs`), so it reads the event log and every gate-run record. The server always passes explicit globs and is unaffected. Verified with ripgrep 15: anchored negations do not apply when the search path is absolute, while unanchored `--glob '!events.jsonl' --glob '!gate-runs'` exclude both and keep absolute result paths, and a user-supplied `--glob` still selects gate-run files. The redo scratch directory can hold appended event bytes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `repository_state/path.rs` declares the data-root history paths (the event log, the gate-run directory and the redo scratch directory) once, beside their `VirtualPath` constants.
- [hard] REQ-02: When neither a glob nor explicit file patterns are given, the search excludes each declared history path; an explicit selection is passed through unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test over a corpus shows that a default search returns no match from a history file and that an explicit glob still reaches one.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. title: Ordinary commands succeed over unparseable history
description:
Prove end to end that ordinary commands never read history: with the event log, the claims log and other issues' gate runs replaced by garbage, issue reads, gate evaluation, claims and lease operations still succeed.

## Background

Only history-reporting commands may read the event log, the claims log or gate-run history. Ordinary commands reach the event log only through the bounded end-of-log probe, the claims log not at all, and gate runs only through the run records their issue's gate state names. No end-to-end test shows this. The CLI integration suite `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/` hosts one module per topic (`main.rs` lists them), and adding a module adds no build target.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One shared fixture creates a git-initialized repository with a target issue and a second issue, defines a gate with a trivial `exec` checker, runs it on the second issue, and acquires and releases one lease so the claims log exists.
- [hard] REQ-02: One shared helper replaces `.jit/events.jsonl` with unparseable lines whose last line is unterminated, replaces `.git/jit/claims.jsonl` with unparseable lines, and overwrites the second issue's gate-run records with unparseable bytes.
- [hard] REQ-03: With that corruption in place, separate tests show that `issue show`, `issue status` and `query available` succeed; that gate evaluation of the target issue succeeds; that `claim acquire` succeeds and appends its claim event; and that lease acquire, renew and release succeed.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: A CLI integration module proves ordinary commands succeed over unparseable history files.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One test module over one shared fixture and one corruption helper.

title: The storage-format reference describes per-key records and history files
description:
Rewrite the storage-format reference and the concepts pages so they describe per-key gate runs, verdict records, archive evidence and lease records, and name the history files with the commands that read them.

## Background

`docs/reference/storage-format.md` describes gate runs as one directory per run (`:31`, `:293-295`), the claims control plane with a `claims.index.json` "derived cache" of `claims.jsonl` (`:377-409`), and no history files or their readers. `docs/concepts/guarantees.md` lists the index in its layout (`:410-420`), draws claim acquisition reading the index (`:128-133`), and states that issue operations read only the log's length and final line (`:638`, `:645`). `docs/concepts/overview.md:99` shows the gate-run tree.

After the restructuring: gate runs are `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json`, the issue's gate state names its latest run, verdict records live at `gate-runs/verdicts/<gate-key>/<inputs-digest>.json`, archive evidence at `archive-evidence/<target-key>.json`, and leases at `.git/jit/leases/<issue-id>.json` with a `claims.seq` counter. The history files are the event log, `claims.jsonl` and the gate-run directories; the history-reporting commands are `jit events`, `jit worktree store-divergence`, `jit gate status --all` and `--limit`, and the server's gate-run list. No command reads `claims.jsonl`, and nothing is derived from a history file.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `storage-format.md` describes each per-key record by path and states that it is written in the same redo record as the change that produces it. Its flat gate-run layout and every "derived cache" or index wording are gone.
- [hard] REQ-02: `storage-format.md` has a history-files section that names each history file and the commands that read it, and states that no ordinary command reads one and no file is derived from one.
- [hard] REQ-03: `guarantees.md` and `overview.md` match the per-key layout, and the log-read statement at `guarantees.md:638` is true.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: The storage-format and concepts pages describe per-key records and name history files and their readers.

title: Gate runs are addressed per issue, per gate and per inputs digest
description:
Gate-run records are stored and read by key, so reading one issue's runs, its latest run of a gate, or a reusable verdict never reads another key's records.

## Background

Gate runs were stored flat, and every reader enumerated and parsed all of them. This story stores runs per issue, names each issue's latest run of a gate on its gate state, finds reusable verdicts through a per-key verdict record, captures only the evaluated issue's latest runs into gate mutations, and rewrites this repository's recorded runs once into that layout.

- [hard] REQ-03: Gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation capture no other issue's run records.
- [hard] REQ-04: This repository's recorded runs, latest-run references and verdict records are in the per-key layout, and every cited run id resolves.

title: Leases are per-issue records under one lease sequence
description:
Each lease is one record changed by one lock-load-change-publish sequence, and claims decide their event from the issue record, so no lease or claim operation reads the claims log or the event log's records.

## Background

The claims control plane kept every lease in one index that was a second authority beside a replayed log, repeated its lock and publish steps in each operation, and kept test-only APIs. The claim command parsed the whole event log to decide its event. This story stores one record per lease, runs every lease operation through one sequence, addresses every lease command by issue, and makes a claim's event follow the assignee.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reading or changing one issue's lease reads only that issue's lease record, and no lease operation reads the claims log.
- [hard] REQ-02: An interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease, and nothing rebuilds lease state from the log.
- [hard] REQ-03: A claim appends its event exactly when the assignee changes and parses no event-log record.
- [hard] REQ-04: This checkout's leases are carried into lease records, and the lease docs describe them.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: Leases are per-issue records under one sequence, and claims decide their event from the assignee.

title: Only history-reporting commands read history files
description:
The event log, the claims log and gate-run history are append-only records that only history-reporting commands read, with one event-log parser, per-target archive evidence and a search that skips history by default.

## Background

Ordinary commands read the event log whole in captures, validation, archive planning and search, and three event-log parsers disagreed on torn lines and retired tags. This story gives the log one parser and one torn-line rule, moves archive evidence to per-target records, limits mutations to the log's bounded end and enforces that limit in the capture layer, excludes history from default search, documents the history files and their readers, and proves the boundary end to end.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Exactly one event-log parser exists, with one torn-line rule and one treatment of retired tags.
- [hard] REQ-02: Archive preview and execute read a target's evidence record once and never read the event log.
- [hard] REQ-03: The capture layer and the redo record admit only the end-of-log probe and the positioned append.
- [hard] REQ-04: An end-to-end test proves ordinary commands succeed over unparseable history files, and the storage references name the history files and their readers.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.

planning.outcome: Only history-reporting commands read history files, and the boundary is enforced, documented and tested.
